layout.title: How a smoke detector works

shows.does: a hand switches it on and a red beam crosses the dark box
smoke from a burning trash can drifts into the box and through the beam
a sensor appears beside the beam and the scattered light lands on it
the sensor glows but the room fills with smoke in silence
a horn appears and its red light flashes as it blares
a ring traced round the smoke detector
dust and specks drift into the box and the horn keeps flashing
a fine mesh ring closes over the vents and the dust stays out
the beam goes dark as the battery dies behind the screen
a battery appears and the horn light blinks a chirp
the battery slides out of the detector
a test button appears and the hand presses it
the hand presses test and the horn light flashes
the smoke detector on the wall with its light flashing

layout.why: A photoelectric smoke detector hangs cut open on a living room wall above a burning trash can, with a hand at its test button; the smoke is followed from the fire up into the vents, across the beam onto the sensor and out as sound from the horn, and then its battery. The camera opens close on the dark box and its beam, steps back to show the fire and the smoke, and ends on the hand pressing test.

sentences.text: If you shine a light across a dark box, you have a smoke detector.
But smoke drifts through the beam, and nothing happens.
So a side sensor catches light the smoke scatters.
But the sensor stays silent while everyone sleeps.
So you add a horn that blares 85 decibels.
This is a photoelectric smoke detector.
But the horn also blares at dust and bugs inside.
So a fine mesh screen keeps them out.
But behind that screen, the battery quietly dies.
So it chirps when the battery runs low.
But a chirp at 3 AM gets the battery pulled.
So you add a test button to check it monthly.
Press test, and the light flashes as it screams.
Congratulations, you built a smoke detector.

recurring.what: a hand at the test button

the sensor makes no sound while everyone sleeps
